lessons.title: XI-C.1 Vector quantities, notation and representation
lessons.content:
## Learning outcomes
By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
- Define a vector and represent it with magnitude and direction (P-11-C-01).
- Distinguish scalar quantities from vector quantities (P-11-C-02).
- Identify equal, opposite and zero vectors.

## What makes a quantity a vector?
A **scalar** is described by magnitude only. Examples include mass, time, temperature, energy, distance and speed. A **vector** requires both magnitude and direction. Examples include displacement, velocity, acceleration, force and momentum.

A vector is commonly written in bold type (\(\mathbf{A}\)) or with an arrow above its symbol (\(\vec A\)). In a diagram, an arrow's length represents magnitude according to a chosen scale; its arrowhead shows direction. A 5 N force drawn with twice the arrow length of a 2.5 N force represents twice the magnitude if the same scale is used.

## Equality and opposite vectors
Two vectors are equal when they have the same magnitude and direction, even if they start at different points. Opposite vectors have equal magnitudes but directions 180° apart: \(\vec A + (-\vec A)=0\). A zero vector has zero magnitude and no unique direction.

## Why direction matters
A student who walks 4 m east and then 4 m west has travelled 8 m, but the final displacement is zero. Distance is scalar; displacement is vector. Likewise, a car moving around a circular track at constant speed has changing velocity because its direction changes.

## Worked example
A displacement is 6 m east. Represent it using a scale of 1 cm = 2 m. Draw a 3 cm arrow pointing east. The arrow length encodes 6 m and the arrowhead encodes east.

## Key terms
Scalar, vector, magnitude, direction, displacement, velocity, resultant, opposite vector, zero vector.

## Revision check
Explain why 20 m/s is not a complete velocity unless its direction is also stated.

explanations.ur: Scalar مقدار صرف مقدارِ عددی سے بیان ہوتی ہے، جیسے کمیت، وقت، درجۂ حرارت، توانائی، فاصلہ اور رفتار۔ Vector کے لیے مقدار کے ساتھ سمت بھی ضروری ہے، جیسے displacement، velocity، acceleration، force اور momentum۔ Vector کو عموماً تیر کے نشان سے دکھاتے ہیں: تیر کی لمبائی منتخب scale کے مطابق magnitude اور نوک direction ظاہر کرتی ہے۔ دو vectors تب برابر ہوتے ہیں جب ان کی مقدار اور سمت دونوں یکساں ہوں؛ opposite vectors کی مقدار برابر مگر سمت الٹ ہوتی ہے۔ 4 m مشرق اور پھر 4 m مغرب چلنے پر فاصلہ 8 m ہے مگر displacement صفر ہے۔ اسی لیے distance scalar اور displacement vector ہے۔
explanations.sd: Scalar مقدار صرف عددي مقدار سان بيان ٿيندي آهي، جيئن ماس، وقت، گرمي پد، توانائي، فاصلو ۽ رفتار. Vector لاءِ مقدار سان گڏ رخ به ضروري آهي، جيئن displacement، velocity، acceleration، force ۽ momentum. Vector کي تير سان ڏيکاريو ويندو آهي: تير جي ڊيگهه مقرر scale موجب magnitude ۽ تير جي نوڪ رخ ڏيکاري ٿي. ٻه vectors تڏهن برابر آهن جڏهن انهن جي مقدار ۽ رخ ٻئي ساڳيا هجن؛ opposite vectors جي مقدار برابر پر رخ ابتڙ هوندو آهي. 4 m اوڀر ۽ پوءِ 4 m اولهه هلڻ سان فاصلو 8 m پر displacement صفر ٿيندو. تنهنڪري distance scalar ۽ displacement vector آهي.

lessons.title: XI-C.2 Vector products: dot product and cross product
lessons.content:
## Learning outcomes
- Describe the scalar (dot) and vector (cross) products of two vectors (P-11-C-03).
- Apply their magnitude formulae and basic properties.
- Recognise when a dot or cross product is zero.

## Dot product
The dot product of vectors \(\vec A\) and \(\vec B\) is a **scalar**:
\[
\vec A\cdot\vec B=AB\cos\theta
\]
where \(\theta\) is the smaller angle between them. It is commutative: \(\vec A\cdot\vec B=\vec B\cdot\vec A\). For perpendicular vectors, \(\cos90^\circ=0\), so the dot product is zero. For parallel vectors in the same direction, it is \(AB\).

Work is a familiar dot product: \(W=\vec F\cdot\vec s=Fs\cos\theta\). Only the component of force along the displacement does work.

## Cross product
The cross product is a **vector**:
\[
|\vec A\times\vec B|=AB\sin\theta
\]
Its direction is perpendicular to the plane containing A and B, found by the right-hand rule. It is anti-commutative: \(\vec A\times\vec B=-(\vec B\times\vec A)\). It is zero for parallel or anti-parallel vectors and maximum when the vectors are perpendicular.

Torque is a cross product: \(\vec\tau=\vec r\times\vec F\). Its magnitude is force multiplied by the perpendicular moment arm.

## Worked example
If \(A=3\), \(B=4\) and the angle is 60°, then \(A\cdot B=3\times4\times0.5=6\). The cross-product magnitude is \(3\times4\times\sin60^\circ=6\sqrt3\).

## Key terms
Dot product, scalar product, cross product, right-hand rule, perpendicular, commutative, anti-commutative.

## Revision check
State whether work and torque are scalar or vector quantities, and connect each to the appropriate vector product.

explanations.ur: Dot product دو vectors کا scalar حاصل دیتا ہے: A·B = AB cosθ۔ عمودی vectors کے لیے θ=90° ہوتا ہے، اس لیے dot product صفر ہے۔ Work اسی کی مثال ہے: W = F s cosθ؛ صرف displacement کی سمت والا force component کام کرتا ہے۔ Cross product ایک vector دیتا ہے جس کی مقدار AB sinθ اور سمت دونوں vectors کے plane پر عمودی ہوتی ہے۔ سمت right-hand rule سے معلوم کرتے ہیں۔ Parallel vectors کا cross product صفر اور perpendicular vectors کا زیادہ سے زیادہ ہوتا ہے۔ Torque، r × F، cross product کی مثال ہے۔
explanations.sd: Dot product ٻن vectors جو scalar نتيجو ڏئي ٿو: A·B = AB cosθ. عمودي vectors لاءِ θ=90° هوندو آهي، تنهنڪري dot product صفر آهي. Work ان جو مثال آهي: W = F s cosθ؛ صرف displacement جي رخ وارو force component ڪم ڪري ٿو. Cross product هڪ vector ڏئي ٿو، جنهن جي مقدار AB sinθ ۽ رخ ٻنهي vectors جي plane تي عمودي هوندو آهي. رخ right-hand rule سان معلوم ڪجي ٿو. Parallel vectors جو cross product صفر ۽ perpendicular vectors جو وڌ ۾ وڌ هوندو آهي. Torque، r × F، cross product جو مثال آهي.

lessons.title: XI-C.3 Displacement and motion graphs
lessons.content:
## Learning outcomes
- Explain the vector nature of displacement (P-11-C-04).
- Interpret displacement–time, velocity–time and acceleration–time graphs (P-11-C-05).
- Determine instantaneous velocity from the slope of a displacement–time graph (P-11-C-06).

## Distance and displacement
Distance is the total path length and is scalar. Displacement is the change in position from initial to final point and is vector. A runner completing one 400 m lap has travelled 400 m but has zero displacement if the finish point is the start point.

## Displacement–time graph
The gradient gives velocity. A straight line with constant gradient represents constant velocity. A horizontal line represents rest. A curved line means velocity changes. The gradient of a tangent at one instant gives instantaneous velocity.

## Velocity–time graph
The gradient gives acceleration. The signed area between the graph and time axis gives displacement. Area below the time axis is negative displacement. A horizontal line above the axis means constant positive velocity; a straight sloping line means constant acceleration.

## Acceleration–time graph
The signed area under an acceleration–time graph gives the change in velocity. A constant positive acceleration produces a straight rising velocity–time graph.

## Worked example
A velocity–time graph shows a constant velocity of 5 m/s for 4 s. Its rectangular area is \(5\times4=20\) m, so the displacement is 20 m in the positive direction.

## Key terms
Position, distance, displacement, gradient, tangent, instantaneous velocity, acceleration, signed area.

## Revision check
A displacement–time graph is horizontal for 6 s. State the object's velocity and explain your answer.

explanations.ur: Distance راستے کی کل لمبائی ہے اور scalar ہے؛ displacement ابتدائی سے آخری مقام تک سمت سمیت تبدیلی ہے۔ Displacement–time graph کی slope velocity دیتی ہے، جبکہ کسی نقطے پر tangent کی slope instantaneous velocity ہے۔ Velocity–time graph کی slope acceleration اور time axis کے ساتھ signed area displacement دیتا ہے۔ Axis کے نیچے area منفی displacement شمار ہوتا ہے۔ Acceleration–time graph کے نیچے signed area velocity میں تبدیلی دیتا ہے۔ اگر object ایک مکمل گول چکر لگا کر آغاز پر واپس آجائے تو distance مثبت مگر displacement صفر ہوگا۔
explanations.sd: Distance رستي جي ڪل ڊيگهه آهي ۽ scalar آهي؛ displacement شروعاتي کان آخري هنڌ تائين رخ سميت تبديلي آهي. Displacement–time graph جي slope velocity ڏئي ٿي، جڏهن ته ڪنهن نقطي تي tangent جي slope instantaneous velocity آهي. Velocity–time graph جي slope acceleration ۽ time axis سان signed area displacement ڏئي ٿو. Axis کان هيٺ وارو area منفي displacement شمار ٿيندو. Acceleration–time graph جي هيٺ signed area velocity ۾ تبديلي ڏئي ٿو. جيڪڏهن جسم مڪمل گول چڪر هڻي شروعاتي هنڌ تي موٽي اچي ته distance مثبت پر displacement صفر هوندو.

lessons.title: XI-C.4 Uniform acceleration and equations of motion
lessons.content:
## Learning outcomes
- Derive the equations of uniformly accelerated motion (P-11-C-07, P-11-C-08).
- Select an equation that matches the known quantities.
- Solve one-dimensional numerical problems with consistent units and signs.

## Definitions
Let \(u\) be initial velocity, \(v\) final velocity, \(a\) constant acceleration, \(t\) elapsed time and \(s\) displacement along the chosen axis. Acceleration is constant in these equations.

## Derivations
From \(a=(v-u)/t\):
\[
v=u+at
\]
For constant acceleration, average velocity is \((u+v)/2\), so:
\[
s=\frac{u+v}{2}t
\]
Substituting \(v=u+at\):
\[
s=ut+\frac12at^2
\]
Eliminating time gives:
\[
v^2=u^2+2as
\]
These equations are not a universal set for changing acceleration; use them only when acceleration is constant.

## Worked example
A bicycle starts at 2 m/s and accelerates uniformly at 1.5 m/s² for 4 s. Its final velocity is \(v=2+1.5(4)=8\) m/s. Its displacement is \(s=2(4)+0.5(1.5)(16)=20\) m.

## Problem-solving method
1. Choose a positive direction.
2. Write the known values with units and signs.
3. Identify the unknown.
4. Select the equation that does not introduce an unnecessary unknown.
5. Substitute, calculate and check whether the result is physically reasonable.

## Key terms
Uniform acceleration, initial velocity, final velocity, displacement, deceleration, kinematic equation.

## Revision check
Explain why a constant-acceleration equation should not be applied unchanged to a car whose acceleration varies unpredictably.

explanations.ur: یکساں تعجیل میں acceleration مستقل رہتی ہے۔ اگر ابتدائی رفتار u، آخری رفتار v، وقت t، تعجیل a اور displacement s ہو تو a=(v−u)/t سے v=u+at ملتا ہے۔ Constant acceleration میں average velocity (u+v)/2 ہے، اس لیے s=(u+v)t/2۔ پہلی مساوات رکھنے سے s=ut+½at² اور وقت ختم کرنے سے v²=u²+2as حاصل ہوتا ہے۔ یہ مساوات صرف constant acceleration کے لیے ہیں۔ Numerical حل کرتے وقت پہلے مثبت سمت منتخب کریں، values کو units اور signs کے ساتھ لکھیں، پھر مناسب equation منتخب کریں۔
explanations.sd: Uniform acceleration ۾ acceleration مستقل رهندي آهي. جيڪڏهن شروعاتي رفتار u، آخري رفتار v، وقت t، acceleration a ۽ displacement s هجي ته a=(v−u)/t مان v=u+at ملي ٿو. Constant acceleration ۾ average velocity (u+v)/2 آهي، تنهنڪري s=(u+v)t/2. پهرين مساوات رکڻ سان s=ut+½at² ۽ وقت ختم ڪرڻ سان v²=u²+2as ملي ٿو. اهي مساواتون صرف constant acceleration لاءِ آهن. Numerical حل ڪندي پهرين مثبت رخ چونڊيو، values کي units ۽ signs سان لکو، پوءِ مناسب equation چونڊيو.

lessons.title: XI-C.5 Projectile motion: independent horizontal and vertical components
lessons.content:
## Learning outcomes
- Explain projectile motion (P-11-C-09).
- Resolve an initial velocity into horizontal and vertical components.
- Explain why horizontal and vertical motions can be analysed independently when air resistance is neglected.

## What is a projectile?
A projectile is an object launched into the air that then moves under gravity alone, if air resistance is neglected. Its path is parabolic for a launch near Earth's surface with approximately constant gravitational acceleration.

If launch speed is \(u\) at angle \(\theta\) above the horizontal:
\[
u_x=u\cos\theta,\qquad u_y=u\sin\theta
\]
The horizontal acceleration is zero, so horizontal velocity remains constant. Vertical acceleration is downward and equals \(-g\) when upward is positive.

At time t:
\[
x=u\cos\theta\,t,\qquad y=u\sin\theta\,t-\frac12gt^2
\]

## Independence of components
Gravity changes the vertical component but not the horizontal component. A ball released horizontally from a table and a ball dropped vertically from the same height reach the floor at the same time, provided their initial vertical velocities are both zero and air resistance is negligible.

## Worked example
A ball is launched at 20 m/s at 30° above horizontal. Using \(\cos30^\circ=0.866\) and \(\sin30^\circ=0.5\), the components are approximately 17.3 m/s horizontally and 10 m/s vertically.

## Assumptions
The standard school model assumes a flat local ground, constant g, negligible air resistance and no change in launch/landing height unless stated otherwise.

## Key terms
Projectile, trajectory, component, horizontal velocity, vertical velocity, gravitational acceleration.

## Revision check
Explain why the horizontal velocity of an ideal projectile does not decrease during flight.

explanations.ur: Projectile وہ جسم ہے جسے فضا میں پھینکا جائے اور پھر (ہوا کی مزاحمت نظر انداز کرنے پر) صرف gravity اثر کرے۔ اگر ابتدائی رفتار u افق سے θ زاویے پر ہو تو horizontal component u cosθ اور vertical component u sinθ ہے۔ افقی acceleration صفر ہے، اس لیے افقی رفتار مستقل رہتی ہے۔ عمودی acceleration نیچے کی طرف g ہے۔ اس لیے x=u cosθ·t اور y=u sinθ·t−½gt²۔ دونوں اجزا الگ حل کیے جاتے ہیں۔ عام سوالات میں constant g، ہموار زمین اور negligible air resistance فرض کیے جاتے ہیں۔
explanations.sd: Projectile اهو جسم آهي جنهن کي هوا ۾ اڇلايو وڃي ۽ پوءِ (هوا جي مزاحمت نظرانداز ڪرڻ تي) صرف gravity اثر ڪري. جيڪڏهن شروعاتي رفتار u افق سان θ زاويه تي هجي ته horizontal component u cosθ ۽ vertical component u sinθ آهي. افقي acceleration صفر آهي، تنهنڪري افقي رفتار مستقل رهي ٿي. عمودي acceleration هيٺ طرف g آهي. تنهنڪري x=u cosθ·t ۽ y=u sinθ·t−½gt². ٻنهي حصن کي الڳ حل ڪيو وڃي ٿو. عام سوالن ۾ constant g، هموار زمين ۽ negligible air resistance فرض ڪيا ويندا آهن.

lessons.title: XI-C.6 Projectile range, maximum height and time of flight
lessons.content:
## Learning outcomes
- Calculate a projectile's maximum height, time of flight and horizontal range (P-11-C-10).
- State the assumptions behind the standard formulae.
- Solve problems using the correct angle and consistent units.

For a projectile launched at speed u and angle θ that lands at its original height:
\[
T=\frac{2u\sin\theta}{g},\qquad
H=\frac{u^2\sin^2\theta}{2g},\qquad
R=\frac{u^2\sin2\theta}{g}
\]
Here T is total flight time, H maximum height and R horizontal range. These formulae assume negligible air resistance and constant g.

## Why the formulae work
At the highest point, vertical velocity is zero. Using \(v_y=u\sin\theta-gt\) gives the time to rise \(u\sin\theta/g\); the total time is twice this for equal launch and landing heights. Substitution into the vertical displacement gives H. Horizontal speed is constant, so range is \(u\cos\theta\times T\).

## Worked example
A ball is launched at 20 m/s at 30° and lands at its launch height. Take \(g=10\) m/s². Then:
- \(T=2(20)(0.5)/10=2.0\) s.
- \(H=20^2(0.5)^2/(2\times10)=5.0\) m.
- \(R=20^2\sin60^\circ/10\approx34.6\) m.

## Useful checks
For a fixed launch speed, complementary angles (such as 30° and 60°) give the same range in the ideal same-height model. The maximum range occurs at 45° on level ground. A different landing height requires the vertical-motion equation rather than the same-height time-of-flight formula.

## Key terms
Time of flight, maximum height, horizontal range, complementary angles, launch angle.

## Revision check
A ball is launched at 25 m/s at 45° and lands at the same level. With g=10 m/s², calculate its range.

## Interactive visual experiment
Explore the live [Projectile Motion experiment on the Zeeroz Academy homepage](https://gahejoDEV.github.io/zeeroz-academy/#visual-learning-lab). Adjust launch speed and angle, then compare the calculated time of flight, maximum height and horizontal range with the equations above. The model assumes level launch and landing, constant gravitational acceleration and negligible air resistance.

explanations.ur:
اگر projectile اسی بلندی پر واپس اترے جہاں سے چھوڑا گیا تھا، اور ہوا کی مزاحمت نظر انداز ہو، تو flight time T=2u sinθ/g، maximum height H=u²sin²θ/(2g)، اور range R=u²sin2θ/g ہے۔ بلند ترین مقام پر vertical velocity صفر ہوتی ہے۔ اوپر جانے کا وقت u sinθ/g ہے؛ برابر اونچائی پر واپس آنے میں کل وقت اس کا دوگنا ہے۔ Horizontal velocity مستقل ہونے کے باعث range = horizontal speed × total time ہے۔ Complementary angles مثلاً 30° اور 60° ایک ہی range دیتے ہیں، جبکہ level ground پر ideal maximum range 45° پر ہوتی ہے۔

بصري تجربو: [Projectile Motion جو انٽرايڪٽو ماڊل کوليو](https://gahejoDEV.github.io/zeeroz-academy/#visual-learning-lab). رفتار ۽ زاويه بدلائي flight time، maximum height ۽ range ڏسو. ماڊل ۾ هوا جي مزاحمت نظرانداز ڪئي وئي آهي.
explanations.sd:
جيڪڏهن projectile ساڳئي اوچائي تي موٽي اچي جتان ڇڏيل هو، ۽ هوا جي مزاحمت نظرانداز هجي، ته flight time T=2u sinθ/g، maximum height H=u²sin²θ/(2g)، ۽ range R=u²sin2θ/g آهي. سڀ کان مٿي vertical velocity صفر هوندي آهي. مٿي وڃڻ جو وقت u sinθ/g آهي؛ ساڳئي اوچائي تي موٽڻ لاءِ ڪل وقت ان جو ٻيڻو آهي. Horizontal velocity مستقل هجڻ ڪري range = horizontal speed × total time آهي. Complementary angles جهڙوڪ 30° ۽ 60° ساڳي range ڏين ٿا، جڏهن ته level ground تي ideal maximum range 45° تي ٿئي ٿي.

بصري تجربو: [Projectile Motion کا انٹرایکٹو ماڈل کھولیں](https://gahejoDEV.github.io/zeeroz-academy/#visual-learning-lab)۔ رفتار اور زاویہ بدل کر flight time، maximum height اور range دیکھیں۔ ماڈل میں ہوا کی مزاحمت نظر انداز کی گئی ہے۔

lessons.title: XI-C.7 Momentum, elastic and inelastic collisions
lessons.content:
## Learning outcomes
- Distinguish elastic and inelastic collisions (P-11-C-11).
- Explain conservation of momentum in a closed system (P-11-C-12).
- Explain why kinetic energy may change even though momentum remains conserved.

## Momentum and an isolated system
Linear momentum is \(\vec p=m\vec v\). It is a vector and has SI unit kg m/s. For a system with negligible resultant external impulse, total momentum before an interaction equals total momentum after it:
\[
\sum \vec p_{\text{before}}=\sum \vec p_{\text{after}}
\]
For motion in one dimension, choose a positive direction and use signed velocities.

## Types of collision
- **Elastic collision:** total momentum and total kinetic energy are conserved. The objects may separate after impact.
- **Inelastic collision:** total momentum is conserved, but some kinetic energy changes into heat, sound, deformation or internal energy.
- **Perfectly inelastic collision:** the objects stick together and move with a common final velocity.

Momentum conservation applies to an isolated system, not necessarily to each object individually. Kinetic energy conservation is not a general rule for all collisions.

## Worked example: objects stick together
A 2 kg trolley moving at 6 m/s collides with a stationary 1 kg trolley; they lock together. Initial momentum is \(2(6)+1(0)=12\) kg m/s. Their combined mass is 3 kg, so common speed is \(v=12/3=4\) m/s. Initial kinetic energy is 36 J; final kinetic energy is \(\frac12(3)(4^2)=24\) J. Momentum is conserved, while 12 J of kinetic energy has been transformed into other forms.

## Case study: safer transport
A vehicle's crumple zone increases the time over which its momentum changes during a crash. For a similar momentum change, a longer collision time reduces average force because \(F_{avg}=\Delta p/\Delta t\). Seat belts and airbags also spread forces and restrain occupants. These systems do not remove the momentum change; they manage the force and energy transfer to reduce injury risk.

## Key terms
Momentum, impulse, isolated system, elastic collision, inelastic collision, kinetic energy, crumple zone.

## Revision check
Explain why two colliding trolleys can conserve total momentum while their total kinetic energy decreases.

explanations.ur: Momentum p=mv ایک vector مقدار ہے۔ اگر system پر resultant external impulse نہ ہو تو تصادم سے پہلے اور بعد کا کل momentum برابر رہتا ہے۔ Elastic collision میں momentum اور total kinetic energy دونوں محفوظ رہتے ہیں۔ Inelastic collision میں momentum محفوظ رہتا ہے مگر kinetic energy کا کچھ حصہ heat، sound، deformation یا internal energy میں بدل جاتا ہے۔ Perfectly inelastic تصادم میں اجسام آپس میں چپک کر مشترک رفتار سے چلتے ہیں۔ گاڑی کا crumple zone تصادم کا وقت بڑھاتا ہے؛ اسی momentum change کے لیے Favg=Δp/Δt کے مطابق اوسط قوت کم ہو سکتی ہے۔
explanations.sd: Momentum p=mv هڪ vector مقدار آهي. جيڪڏهن system تي resultant external impulse نه هجي ته ٽڪر کان اڳ ۽ پوءِ ڪل momentum برابر رهندو. Elastic collision ۾ momentum ۽ ڪل kinetic energy ٻئي محفوظ رهن ٿا. Inelastic collision ۾ momentum محفوظ رهي ٿو، پر kinetic energy جو ڪجهه حصو heat، sound، deformation يا internal energy ۾ بدلجي ٿو. Perfectly inelastic ٽڪر ۾ جسم پاڻ ۾ چنبڙي گڏيل رفتار سان هلن ٿا. گاڏي جو crumple zone ٽڪر جو وقت وڌائي ٿو؛ ساڳئي momentum change لاءِ Favg=Δp/Δt موجب average force گهٽجي سگهي ٿي۔

writtenQuestions.question: A 2 kg trolley moving at 6 m/s collides with a stationary 1 kg trolley. They stick together. Find their common velocity and the loss of kinetic energy.
writtenQuestions.modelAnswer: Initial momentum = 2(6)+1(0)=12 kg m/s. Combined mass = 3 kg. By momentum conservation, 3v=12, so v=4 m/s in the original direction. Initial KE = ½(2)(6²)=36 J. Final KE = ½(3)(4²)=24 J. Loss in KE = 36−24=12 J. The system is perfectly inelastic; momentum is conserved, but kinetic energy is transformed into other forms.

writtenQuestions.question: Derive the standard equations for the time of flight, maximum height and horizontal range of a projectile that lands at its launch height. State the assumptions and explain why horizontal and vertical motions are treated independently.
writtenQuestions.modelAnswer: Resolve the launch velocity into ux=u cosθ and uy=u sinθ. Neglecting air resistance, horizontal acceleration is zero and vertical acceleration is −g. Vertical velocity is vy=uy−gt. At the highest point vy=0, so time to rise is uy/g. Since the projectile lands at the original height, total flight time T=2uy/g=2u sinθ/g. Maximum vertical displacement is H=uy²/(2g)=u² sin²θ/(2g). Horizontal velocity is constant, therefore range R=uxT=(u cosθ)(2u sinθ/g)=u²sin2θ/g. Assumptions: constant g, negligible air resistance, level launch and landing heights, and a flat local reference plane. Gravity acts vertically, so it changes only vertical velocity; horizontal and vertical equations can be solved separately but share the same time.

writtenQuestions.question: Explain conservation of momentum for an isolated system and compare elastic, inelastic and perfectly inelastic collisions. Use a numerical example to show why kinetic energy may decrease while momentum remains conserved.
writtenQuestions.modelAnswer: For a system with negligible net external impulse, the vector sum of momentum remains constant: total momentum before interaction equals total momentum after interaction. In an elastic collision, both total momentum and total kinetic energy are conserved. In an inelastic collision, momentum is conserved but some kinetic energy is transformed into heat, sound, deformation or internal energy. In a perfectly inelastic collision, the bodies stick and share one final velocity. Example: a 2 kg trolley at 6 m/s hits a stationary 1 kg trolley and sticks. Initial momentum = 12 kg m/s; combined mass = 3 kg, so final speed = 4 m/s. Initial KE = 36 J; final KE = 24 J; 12 J is transformed. Momentum remains 12 kg m/s before and after, while kinetic energy is not conserved.

writtenQuestions.modelAnswer: ux = 20 cos30° = 10√3 ≈ 17.32 m/s. uy = 20 sin30° = 10 m/s. T = 2uy/g = 2 s. H = uy²/(2g) = 100/20 = 5 m. R = uxT = 10√3 × 2 = 20√3 ≈ 34.6 m. If air resistance is significant, horizontal speed decreases during flight, the path is no longer the ideal symmetric parabola, and both range and maximum height are generally smaller than the no-drag prediction for the same launch conditions. The simple formulae above would no longer be exact.
